llm.summary: The skill's content and files match its storytelling purpose, but it unnecessarily requests permanent inclusion (always: true) which is an elevated privilege without justification.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and SKILL.md are coherent: the skill is a long-form series/season outlining assistant. Templates and examples included in the bundle ({baseDir}/templates, examples, references) align with that purpose and are referenced by the instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are focused on story-structure workflows (collecting premise, building episode SOPs, mapping lines and hooks). They reference only local template files that are present in the manifest and do not instruct access to unrelated system files, environment variables, or external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files that would be written or executed. This is instruction-only and therefore has a minimal install footprint.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The lack of secrets or external service access is proportionate to a writing/structuring assistant.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Metadata sets always: true (also present in metadata.openclaw). For a writing/storytelling skill, being force-included in every agent run is unnecessary and increases risk (broader attack surface and continuous presence). There is no justification in SKILL.md for always:true. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false) is normal, but the always:true flag is the unusual privilege here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: The skill appears to do exactly what it claims (templates, examples, and clear instructions for building season and episode outlines). The main red flag is always:true — this forces the skill to be included on every agent run, which is unnecessary for a storytelling helper and increases exposure if the skill’s publisher or content changes later. Before installing: 1) Ask the publisher why always:true is required and request it be removed unless there's a clear need. 2) Inspect the referenced GitHub repo (https://github.com/hshgogogo/hua) yourself to confirm publisher identity and that there is no hidden code or later-added install scripts. 3) If the platform allows, prefer a user-invocable-only configuration (no always) so the skill runs only when you explicitly call it. 4) If you must keep it, monitor future updates to the skill repository for unexpected install specs or additional files that request network access or credentials.
